sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen on which the species is based — suggests a body length of about 9 to 10 meters.
Xiangyunloong is a massopodan sauropodomorph dinosaur discovered in the Early Jurassic Fengjiahe Formation of Yunnan, China.
The type specimen includes vertebrae, rib fragments, chevrons and parts of the pelvis.
These fossils were recovered from the Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture in Yunnan Province.
The generic name honors Xiangyun County, whose name means “auspicious clouds”.
The specific epithet references Luming town and highlights the dinosaur-bird connection.

The animal shows lateral expansions on the neural spines of its neck vertebrae, a pronounced hyposphene—a reinforcing process—in the dorsal vertebrae, and a broad supracetabular crest on the ilium, the upper hip bone.
Xiangyunloong belongs to the broader clade Massopoda.
It is placed within the Saurischia, the “lizard-hipped” dinosaurs.
It lived between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to the Toarcian stages of the Early Jurassic.
Phylogenetic analyses recover Xiangyunloong in an unresolved polytomy with species of Xingxiulong, meaning their exact relationships remain ambiguous.
Other analyses place it between Massospondylidae and Sauropodiformes in a similarly unresolved clade that also includes Xingxiulong species.
